transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you for seeing me. Um... well, I guess I've just been feeling a little overwhelmed lately, if that's okay to say. 

I just keep feeling like... like I’ve really let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It’s probably silly to get so worked up over it, but every time I make even a small mistake at work—I wait tables, so it happens—it just feels like proof that I’m kind of useless. It just makes me feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

I know I shouldn't be so negative, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just in here complaining... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Um... no, I don't think so. Not about just anything, anyway. I mean, I definitely stress about the mortgage and work, like I mentioned, but... well, there's a clear reason for those, right? I try really hard not to be someone who just worries over nothing. I don't want to make things harder on anyone else by overreacting. 

I hope that's a good answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?

Um... well, I guess I have been, a little bit. I really try not to let it show, especially at work, because I don't want to bring anyone else down. But... yeah, most days there's just this... this heavy, kind of empty feeling right in my chest. 

It's like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I carry the plates, I smile at the customers because I know I'm supposed to, but... I don't really feel anything good behind it. I'm just pretending, I guess. I really hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for my job or anything like that. I know I should be more positive. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do these feelings seem mainly connected to the mortgage and work stress?

Um... well, it's definitely connected to that, but... I don't know, maybe this sounds silly, and I really hope you don't think I'm being dramatic. But... sometimes it feels like it's more than just normal stress? 

Like... I just can't shake this feeling that the bank, and... and sometimes even my manager, are just... watching me? Like they're waiting for me to mess up so they can take everything away. I know my coworkers try to tell me it's fine, like if there's a small error on the register or some paperwork thing, they show me it's just a normal mistake. And I nod and agree because I don't want to seem difficult or crazy, but... inside, I still feel like it's a test, or like they're building a case against me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really paranoid and weird. I try really hard to just ignore it and do my job. Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes? I hope I'm explaining it right.
When your coworkers show you that a mistake was normal, do you still believe the bank or your manager is deliberately building a case against you?

Um... well... I guess, yeah, I do still kind of believe it. I know I shouldn't, and I really don't want to be difficult when my coworkers are being so nice and trying to help me. I always thank them and tell them they're right, because I don't want them to think I'm ungrateful or... or crazy. 

But... yeah, deep down, I just can't shake the feeling. Even when they show me the receipt or the paperwork and it's just a normal error... I still feel like the bank or my manager are just waiting and watching for me to mess up so they can take everything. I know it sounds bad, and I'm really sorry if that's not the right way to think about it. I try to push it away, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too unreasonable.
Do you believe it is actually true that your manager or the bank are watching you and building a case against you?

Um... well... yes. I mean, I try not to, but... I do. I really do believe it. It's just... I can't shake the feeling that they're watching me, waiting for me to make a mistake. Even when my coworkers are so nice and show me that it was just a normal register error or a paperwork thing... I just can't let it go. 

I know it probably makes me sound like a terrible employee, or like I'm completely losing my mind. I really don't want you to think badly of me. I know I should just trust my coworkers when they tell me it's fine. But it feels so real to me. Is that... is that really bad? I'm sorry, I'm trying so hard to be normal about all this.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Um... well... I guess... sometimes? I mean, I don't want you to think I'm completely crazy, and I know it's probably just the stress playing tricks on me. But... yeah, sometimes when I'm closing up the restaurant late at night, or when I'm just sitting all alone in the condo... I'll hear this low voice. 

It's usually just whispering my name, or... or saying that I'm going to lose everything. And I know there's no one there, I really do. But it sounds so real that I actually turn around to check. I always feel so silly afterward. I'm sure it's just because I'm tired, right? Like, it's normal to hear things when you're really exhausted and stressed out? I hope that doesn't make me sound too unstable.
Do you hear that whisper only when you’re feeling down?

Um... well, no... not exactly. I mean, I know it would probably make more sense if it only happened when I was really depressed, and I wish I could say it did. But... there was this one stretch recently, maybe for a few weeks? I was actually feeling a bit better. My mood wasn't so down, and I was getting through my shifts at the restaurant a lot easier. I was trying really hard to be positive.

But... I still heard the whispering when I was alone at the condo. And I still felt like I was being watched, especially when I looked at the mortgage paperwork. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really strange that it happens even when I'm feeling okay. I hope that doesn't mean something worse is wrong with me? I'm really trying my best to handle it all.
Has there been a time when the whispering or the feeling of being watched lasted for at least two weeks while you were not feeling depressed?

Um... yes, exactly. Like I was just mentioning... I'm sorry if I didn't explain it clearly a second ago, I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. But yes, that stretch I brought up... it definitely lasted for at least two or three weeks. 

I was actually doing really well! My mood wasn't down at all, and I was getting through my shifts at the restaurant so much better. I was really proud of myself for holding it together. But... yeah, even during those couple of weeks when I wasn't depressed, I still heard the whispering when I was at the condo. And I still felt like they were watching me over the mortgage paperwork. 

I know it doesn't make a lot of sense to have those things happen when I'm actually in a good mood... I hope I'm explaining this right for you? Does that make sense?
Have there been times during all of this when you were depressed for most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Um... well, yes. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, because I know I still have a job and I should be grateful. But... yeah, there have definitely been times like that. 

For a while now, most days there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It's like I'm just going through the motions at the restaurant, you know? I'm carrying plates, and I'm smiling at the customers because I know I'm supposed to, and I really try to be a good server. But I'm not smiling because I actually feel anything good inside. It's just... exhausting, pretending all the time. 

And that definitely goes on for weeks at a time. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm just lazy or not trying hard enough to be happy? I do try, I promise. I just... it's hard to shake that empty feeling. Does that sound like what you were asking about?
